text: A director leans in: how do we know there isn't a third system out there that disagrees with both of these? Howard's honest answer isn't certainty — it's a process: the dual-check layer is now standing, and a new 30-day sweep checks for grants that bypass normal channels entirely.

A second director asks the harder version: why did it take a script to catch what an audit should have caught? Mara reframes it without dodging — the audit covered the common case, the automation was built for the uncommon case. Two scopes, used together on purpose.

Neither answer claims the problem is solved forever. Both describe a specific, checkable process and are honest about exactly where confidence runs out. That's what survives a follow-up question, instead of collapsing under one.

The general principle: when a hard question comes from someone non-technical, show the process behind your confidence, and name its real boundary honestly. Next lesson turns from defending this phase to planning the next one.
